chunks: Then He placed the keys of His treasuries in your hands, in the sense that He showed you the way to ask Him,
so whenever you wish, you open the doors of His favor with prayer, and draw down the abundant showers of His mercy,
so do not let the delay of His response discourage you, for the gift is according to the measure of the intention,
and sometimes the response is delayed for you, so that this may be a greater reward for the asker, and more generous for the gift of the expectant.
and sometimes you ask for a thing but it is not given to you, and a better thing is given to you, either soon or late,
or it is turned away from you for what is better for you, for there is a matter which you sought, in which is the ruin of your religion if it were given to you,
so let your request be for that which remains for you with its beauty, and its burden is removed from you;
As for wealth, it will not last for you, nor will you live for it.
ai.seo_question: Why does God delay answering prayers according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this instruction to his son Hasan following the Battle of Siffin, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) contextualizes divine response within the framework of *hikmah* (wisdom), explaining that delays in supplication are often merciful delays to increase reward or ward off unseen harm. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the distinction between *istijab* (acceptance) and *isti'jab* (being made worthy of acceptance), urging the believer to seek eternal spiritual beauty over transient material wealth.
